passage.full_text:
Paragraph 1 — Darkness after sunset
In 2014, in many villages in Africa, people have no electricity. When the sun goes down, it is very dark. People use candles or oil lamps. These are dangerous. Children study with bad light. They hurt their eyes.

Paragraph 2 — Solar lamps arrive
A group brings solar lamps to the villages. The lamps are small and cost 10 dollars each. During the day, the lamps get sunlight. At night, they give bright light. Families buy the lamps. One lamp lights the whole house.

Paragraph 3 — Children study at night
Now children can study after dark. They read books under the bright light. Their marks get better. They stay in school longer. Parents are very happy. They say the lamp changed their child's future.

Paragraph 4 — More than light
Solar lamps do more than light homes. Mothers can sew at night. Shopkeepers can work longer hours. The lamps are safe. There are no fires. The lamps are cheap to use. After one year, the lamp pays for itself.

Paragraph 5 — Villages shine at night
Now 30,000 families use solar lamps. The villages are safer at night. Criminals stay away from lit homes. Children's health is better. People sleep better. A simple solar lamp brought big changes to poor communities.
